title: Marrying Dialogue Systems with Data Visualization: Interactive Data Visualization Generation from Natural Language Conversations

problem.claim: Users need support for constructing complex data visualizations through consecutive exchanges involving dataset questions, data manipulation, and visualization.

gap.claim: Existing text-to-visualization approaches assume a well-organized natural-language question expressed in a single sentence and do not address conversational visualization construction.

contributions.claim: Introduces Conversational text-to-Visualization (CoVis), a task for constructing data visualizations through user-system interactions.
Builds Dial-NVBench, a benchmark dataset containing dialogue sessions with sequences of user queries and system responses aimed at creating a suitable visualization.
Proposes MMCoVisNet, a multimodal neural network that understands dialogue context and uses adaptive text, SQL-form, and visualization-form decoders for different response types.

author_reported_evidence.claim: MMCoVisNet is comparatively evaluated against other baselines on the proposed benchmark dataset.
The authors report that MMCoVisNet outperforms existing baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data visualization is presented as an effective tool for illustrating insights, motivating efforts to lower the barrier to its use.
Single-sentence text-to-visualization methods do not match real-world needs for complex visualizations developed through consecutive exchanges.
The paper defines CoVis and introduces Dial-NVBench with dialogue sessions covering multiple visualization-related query types.
MMCoVisNet models dialogue context and selects adaptive decoders for general text, data queries, and visualization construction.
The model is compared with baselines, and the authors report superior and state-of-the-art performance.

source_observation.claim: Conversational visualization requires handling heterogeneous requests, including information seeking, data manipulation, and visualization.

interpretation.claim: A useful conversational analytics system may need distinct response modes rather than a single uniform generation pathway.

application.claim: Design interactive data tools with dialogue-state understanding and specialized outputs for explanatory text, structured queries, and visual specifications.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether specialized decoders are necessary for all conversational visualization settings.

unknowns: Dataset size, domains, annotation process, and train-validation-test protocol are not specified.
Evaluation metrics, baseline identities, and quantitative results are not provided.
Model architecture details and implementation requirements are not described.
